Interested in coding, technology, creative problem-solving and space exploration, I'm excited to collaborate on our Space Mission Design Game for NASA Space Apps Challenge.

We're looking for creative and enthusiastic teammates interested in coding, game development, UI/UX, design, animation or space science. No expertise required, just curiosity, teamwork and a willingness to learn!
summary:
SAVE THE MOON is an interactive educational simulation that puts players in the role of a lunar mission commander. Players must manage limited resources, select suitable spacecraft power systems, and respond to unexpected challenges such as lunar dust storms and communication failures.

The project transforms complex space mission concepts into an engaging decision-making experience. Through multiple mission stages, players balance spacecraft power, budget, system integrity and scientific data collection. Their decisions influence mission performance and the final mission evaluation.

Inspired by NASA's lunar exploration programmes and real spacecraft engineering concepts, SAVE THE MOON aims to make space science more accessible while encouraging critical thinking, resource management and problem-solving. It provides students and space enthusiasts with an opportunity to explore the challenges involved in planning and operating a lunar mission.
details:
Project Overview

SAVE THE MOON is an interactive lunar mission commander simulation designed to introduce users to the challenges of spacecraft operations and lunar exploration.

How It Works

The simulation begins with a mission briefing in which players take responsibility for a spacecraft operating around the Moon. Players progress through three major decision stages followed by a mission evaluation.

  • Power Architecture: Players select a suitable power system while considering available resources and spacecraft requirements.
  • Dust Storm Emergency: Players respond to lunar dust-related hazards and make decisions to protect spacecraft operations.
  • Communication Blackout: Players decide how to handle communication interruptions and maintain mission operations.
  • Mission Evaluation: The simulation evaluates mission performance based on the decisions made throughout the experience.

The mission dashboard tracks important indicators, including mission budget, spacecraft power, scientific data and system integrity.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project provides an interactive learning environment where users can understand how engineering decisions affect space missions. It encourages critical thinking, resource management, problem-solving and interest in lunar exploration.

Creativity and Innovation

Instead of presenting space mission concepts only through theory, SAVE THE MOON allows users to experience them through decision-based gameplay. The combination of resource allocation, emergency scenarios and mission evaluation makes learning more engaging.

Development Considerations

The team considered spacecraft power requirements, limited mission resources, lunar environmental hazards, communication reliability and scientific objectives while designing the simulation.

The project is an educational simulation inspired by real space exploration concepts, rather than an official NASA simulator or a scientifically validated spacecraft operations model.
